title: Strict-local smooth transfer for constant affine-line sections
statement:
Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field, $\ell$ a prime invertible in $k$, and $B$ a finite abelian group killed by a power of $\ell$. Let $R$ be a strictly henselian local $k$-algebra (henselian local with separably closed residue field) [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology], and put $S=\operatorname{Spec}R$, $C=\mathbf A^1_k$ and $C_S=\mathbf A^1_S$ [def-sbc-affine-space]. Write $g:S\to\operatorname{Spec}k$, $f:C\to\operatorname{Spec}k$, $h:C_S\to C$ and $e:C_S\to S$ for the projections of their Cartesian square. All coefficient sheaves are constant sheaves [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. Use the small etale sites [def-weil-pbc-etale-site], the bounded-below abelian derived categories [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], direct images [def-weil-pbc-direct-image], and inverse-image units [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image]. Then the canonical unit
$$B_C[0]\longrightarrow Rh_*B_{C_S}[0]$$
is an isomorphism. Under the ordinary derived-sections composition comparison, its image is the canonical pullback isomorphism
$$h^*:R\Gamma(C_{\mathrm{et}},B_C)\xrightarrow{\sim}R\Gamma((C_S)_{\mathrm{et}},B_{C_S}).$$
This map preserves constants: the composite of $B[0]\to R\Gamma(C,B_C)$ with $h^*$ equals the constants map $B[0]\to R\Gamma(C_S,B_{C_S})$. There is no finite-type, Noetherian or dimension hypothesis on $R$.

source.place: Tags 0EYU, theorem-smooth-base-change, and 03QO, lemma-vanishing-etale-cohomology-strictly-henselian; blueprint Reduction to a geometric fibre, with smooth side f and qcqs side g, not smoothness of the affine-line projection over S as an arbitrary-base-change assertion.

proof.text: Put $P=\operatorname{Spec}k$. The square in the statement is Cartesian since $R\otimes_k k[t]=R[t]$. By [sbc-lem-affine-space-smooth], $f:C\to P$ is smooth. The map $g:\operatorname{Spec}R\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is affine: its inverse image over the sole nonempty affine open of $P$ is $S$, which is affine. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence] makes $g$ quasi-compact and quasi-separated. By [lem-kun-pullback-constant] all inverse images of the constant coefficient sheaves in this square are canonically the corresponding constant sheaves. These identifications are induced by constant sections. Every element of $B$ is killed by $\ell^a$ for some fixed $a$, and $\ell^a$ is a unit on $P$, so $B_S$ satisfies the torsion hypothesis of smooth base change.

source.place: Tag 0EYU, theorem-smooth-base-change: verification of the square; Tags 00T7 and 01V5 for affine space

proof.text: For a nonzero local ring every prime is contained in its unique maximal ideal, so every nonempty closed subset of its spectrum contains the closed point. A partition into two clopen subsets therefore has an empty part. Consequently $S$ and $P$ are connected and nonempty. By [lem-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf-sections-connected] the actual constant-section maps $B\to\Gamma(S,B_S)$ and $B\to\Gamma(P,B_P)$ are isomorphisms. By [lem-weil-pbc-strictly-henselian-etale-acyclic], $H^q(S,B_S)=0$ for $q>0$. The same node applied to the field $k$ says that $\Gamma(P,-)$ is exact: a field is henselian (a simple residue root already lies in the field), and the algebraically closed field $k$ is separably closed. By [lem-weil-pbc-geometric-point-cohomology], for every geometric point $\bar p$ of $P$ the germ map $\Gamma(P,F)\to F_{\bar p}$ is an isomorphism for every abelian sheaf $F$. Thus a map whose global sections are bijective is bijective on all these stalks; alternatively the identity geometric point already realizes global sections.

Let $I$ be an injective resolution of $B_S$ in nonnegative degrees. By [def-weil-pbc-direct-image], $g_*I$ represents $Rg_*B_S$ and $\Gamma(P,g_*I)=\Gamma(S,I)$. Exactness of $\Gamma(P,-)$ and [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-complex-cohomology] identify $\Gamma(P,\mathcal H^q(g_*I))$ with $H^q(S,B_S)$. The adjunction unit $a:B_P[0]\to Rg_*B_S[0]$ is represented by $B_P[0]\to g_*I$: first pull back constant sections, then apply $B_S\to I$. On global sections this induces the isomorphism $B\to\Gamma(S,B_S)$ in degree zero from step 2, and an isomorphism between zero groups in all other degrees. Step 2 identifies these global-section maps with every geometric stalk map. Apply [lemma-weil-pbc-geometric-stalk-conservative] to each cohomology sheaf map: all are isomorphisms. The representing map of complexes is therefore a quasi-isomorphism and is inverted in the derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Hence the specified unit $a$ is an isomorphism.

source.place: Tags 03QO and 03PU, theorem-exactness-stalks (stalk criterion), using the resolution computation of higher direct images

proof.text: Let $\beta=f^{-1}Rg_*B_S[0]\to Rh_*e^{-1}B_S[0]$ be the derived exchange of [sbc-def-base-change-map], specialized to abelian sheaves ($\Lambda=\mathbf Z$). Its $q$-th cohomology map is precisely $f^{-1}R^qg_*B_S\to R^qh_*e^{-1}B_S$, as that definition specifies. By [sbc-thm-smooth-base-change] and the hypotheses verified in step 1 this map is invertible for every $q\geq0$. For $q<0$ both sides vanish, since the sheaf is in degree zero, direct image is right derived, and inverse image is exact. Thus $\beta$ is invertible: represent it by a map from its source to an injective representative of its target; that map induces isomorphisms on all cohomology sheaves, hence is a quasi-isomorphism [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Consequently $\beta\circ f^{-1}a:B_C[0]\to Rh_*B_{C_S}[0]$ is invertible.

source.place: Tag 0EYU, theorem-smooth-base-change; canonical derived exchange and its cohomology maps

proof.text: We identify the last composite with the actual unit $\eta_h$. The transpose formula in [sbc-def-base-change-map] says that its transpose under $h^{-1}\dashv Rh_*$ is, after the square identification, $e^{-1}(\varepsilon_g\circ g^{-1}\eta_g)$ evaluated on $B_P[0]$. Here $a=\eta_{g,B_P[0]}$ and $g^{-1}B_P=B_S$. The triangle identity gives $\varepsilon_{g,g^{-1}B_P}\circ g^{-1}\eta_{g,B_P}=\mathrm{id}_{g^{-1}B_P}$. Its inverse image along $e$ is $\mathrm{id}_{B_{C_S}[0]}$. The transpose of $\eta_h$ is the same identity by the unit formula for an adjunction. Equality of transposes gives $\beta\circ f^{-1}a=\eta_h$. Thus the unit in the statement is invertible.

source.place: Tag 0EYU with the unit-counit definition of exchange; triangle identity

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback-derived-unit] with $u=h$ and $K=B_C[0]$. Its Leray isomorphism identifies $R\Gamma(C,Rh_*B_{C_S})$ with $R\Gamma(C_S,B_{C_S})$, and its clause (2) identifies $R\Gamma(C,\eta_h)$ followed by this isomorphism with the canonical pullback $h^*$. Since functors preserve isomorphisms, this is an isomorphism. To check constants as a derived morphism, choose a nonnegative injective resolution $s:B_C\to J$ and a K-injective resolution $r:h^{-1}J\to I$, taking $t:B_{C_S}\to I$ to be $r\circ h^{-1}s$. This is exactly the resolution recipe in [def-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback]. The pullback recipe [def-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback] is the map $\Gamma(C,J)\to\Gamma(C_S,I)$ induced by the inverse-image unit and that comparison. Precomposing with $B[0]\to\Gamma(C,J)$ sends $b$ to $t(b)$, because $r\circ h^{-1}s=t$ and the inverse image of a constant section $b$ is the same constant section by [lem-weil-pbc-sets-etale-inverse-image-constant-sheaf]. This is exactly the constants map $B[0]\to\Gamma(C_S,I)$. Thus the two maps agree already on these complexes, and hence in $D^+(\mathrm{Ab})$.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q153-5bb71ccab (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: Read the item, its six steps and every cited statement. The delivery has no new nodes and leaves the statement unchanged. It follows the main-20261015 sk-prop-a1-kummer 'Reduction to a geometric fibre' paragraph, and the route uses no SGA. Smooth base change (Stacks 0EYU, l.17446) is applied in the right orientation: the smooth arrow is f: A^1_k -> Spec k and the qcqs arrow is g: Spec R -> Spec k. In sbc-thm-smooth-base-change terms, X=C, S=P, T=Spec R, Y=C_S. The torsion hypothesis holds because l^a kills B_S. Step 2: connectedness is elementary. 03QO acyclicity (l.8207) needs no Noetherian hypothesis, and the natural germ isomorphism on Spec k checks out. Step 3: the unit is represented through adjunction clause (2) and the exact functor Gamma(P,-) is moved past H^q. Global sections are identified with stalks and stalk conservativity gives a quasi-isomorphism. Step 4: BC^q is H^q of the derived exchange by definition, and q<0 is trivial. Step 5 has one gap: the cited square nodes do not say how theta acts on constant sections. So 'equals eta_h' holds only up to Rh_* of an isomorphism, but invertibility of the stated unit follows anyway. Step 6: Leray and the derived-unit clause (2) give the pullback, and the constants are checked on representing complexes via the unique constant-section iso. Small cases tested: R=k, B=0, nonreduced R, non-Noetherian R. The DAG and blueprint duplicate search found only the G_m Kummer node, which is not a duplicate. The generic tool_uses are accepted. Step 2's reason that a field is henselian is worded loosely but the claim is true; no change made.
